claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is a high-entropy alloy.
CoCrFeMnNi components can be fabricated by laser powder bed fusion.
Conventional fixed-parameter LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi produces porosity, dimensional deviations, and residual stresses.
The proposed intervention is a real-time machine-learning closed-loop system that uses in-situ sensor feedback to modulate laser power.
Dynamic laser-power modulation will reduce melt-pool instabilities during LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi.
Dynamic laser-power modulation will reduce residual-stress buildup during LPBF of CoCrFeMnNi.
Reducing melt-pool instabilities and residual-stress buildup will improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects.
Dynamically adjusted laser-energy input stabilizes the melt pool.
Dynamically adjusted laser-energy input minimizes rapid thermal gradients.
Melt-pool stabilization and reduced thermal gradients reduce the formation or propagation of porosity and residual stresses.
Real-time measurements of melt-pool temperature or bead geometry can be used by a machine-learning model to predict optimal laser-power adjustments.
Predicted laser-power adjustments control melt-pool dynamics and solidification behavior.
Control of melt-pool dynamics and solidification behavior yields tighter dimensional tolerances and enhanced mechanical properties.
Relative to fixed-parameter LPBF, closed-loop control will reduce geometric deviations, increase strength, and lower defect density.
The intervention will be effective within standard LPBF operational windows for CoCrFeMnNi.
Performance may vary with sensor quality, machine-learning model accuracy, powder characteristics, and other process variables.

Failure to achieve a statistically significant dimensional improvement of at least approximately 5% together with a mechanical-property improvement of approximately 10% or a significant defect-density reduction is designated as falsifying evidence.
